---
title: "Processor migration to Cloudflare"
description: "Per-job plan and cost bounds for moving scheduled processors off Vercel, with checkout expiry as the Worker template."
updatedAt: '2026-10-23'
---

Moving a job's **schedule** into [Cron Control](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control)
still invokes its Vercel function every slot. Moving its **processor** into a
Worker, Queue consumer or Workflow removes that invocation. Follow
[Cloudflare backend ownership](/build/devops/cloudflare-backend-ownership) and the
[runaway-work acceptance](/build/development-tools/oxc-cloudflare-adoption#runaway-work-and-cost-acceptance)
rules for every move.

## Template: checkout expiry Worker processor

`apps/cron-control/src/processors/checkout-expiry.ts` ports Inventory's
checkout-expiry processor. It runs only when `inventory-checkout-expiry` is in
both `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` and `CRON_CONTROL_WORKER_PROCESSORS`, so the
schedule can move first and the processor later. Both vars are empty by default.

- **Same claim.** The Worker calls the private `expire_inventory_checkout_sessions`
  RPC directly with the service key in `apikey`. The RPC locks candidates with
  `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and only moves `reserved` rows, so a concurrent legacy
  run cannot double-expire a checkout.
- **Same bounds.** At most 10 batches of 1,000 rows per slot, one shared `p_now`,
  30-second database deadlines and manual redirects. The ledger stop fence is
  checked before every batch after the first.
- **One deadline inside the lease.** A Worker processor gets an absolute deadline
  30 seconds before its slot lease expires (240 seconds for checkout expiry's
  270-second lease). Every request uses its fixed timeout capped by the time left,
  and none starts with under a second remaining, so the run always finishes and
  records its outcome before a later slot can claim.
- **Next-only side effect.** Storefront payloads are cached for a year and
  invalidated by tag inside the Next.js host. When rows expire, the Worker posts
  their workspace ids, 100 per request, to `POST /api/cron/inventory/checkout-expiry`
  with Inventory's cron secret. That handler only revalidates; it accepts at most
  100 UUIDs in an 8 KiB body. Committed expiries are revalidated even if a later
  batch fails. Affected workspace ids are persisted on the job's ledger row as a
  pending obligation before revalidation, and each accepted chunk settles its
  ids. A failed or deadline-deferred revalidation fails (or defers) the slot, and
  every later sweep retries the outstanding obligations first, so a storefront is
  never left stale after a transient Inventory error.
- **Outcomes.** A database deadline is `unknown`; HTTP errors, redirects and an
  unexpected RPC shape are `failed`. Worker processors run once per slot: the next
  slot is the retry, and five consecutive failed slots stop the job.

**Cost.** An idle slot is two ledger requests and one RPC, with no Vercel call:
at 288 slots a day that removes 288 Inventory function invocations and adds 288
database RPCs (the Next route made the same RPC). A full slot is at most 10 RPCs
plus one revalidation request per 100 affected workspaces.

**Cutover.** Enable the job first (it calls the Next route), verify one slot, then
add it to `CRON_CONTROL_WORKER_PROCESSORS` in a separate change. Verify one slot
with `detail.expired` and storefront freshness for a test checkout, then remove the
Vercel cron. Roll back by removing the id from `CRON_CONTROL_WORKER_PROCESSORS`;
the job returns to calling the Next route.

Regression coverage: `src/processors/checkout-expiry.test.ts` counts RPC and
revalidation calls for idle, draining, capped, stopped, partially failed, deadline,
malformed and chunked cases; `src/dispatch.test.ts` proves the port runs only when
selected; the Inventory route test covers revalidation auth and input bounds.

## Per-job plan

| Job | Processor target | Work bounds to keep | Cost change when moved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory-checkout-expiry` | Worker processor (implemented, off) | 10 × 1,000 rows, revalidation chunks of 100 | −288 Vercel invocations a day |
| `tasks-cleanup-media` | Worker processor with a durable workspace cursor in the ledger | Page storage listings, bound workspaces per slot, keep the 30-day retention and reference checks | −1 long (300 s) invocation a day; deletes stay idempotent |
| `pay-products` | Worker processor | Page Polar products at 100, keep upsert by provider id | −2 a day |
| `infrastructure-sync-trust-cache` | Worker processor writing the trust cache over REST | Keep 32-way write concurrency and the 2-hour TTL | −144 a day |
| `calendar-provider-sync` | Queue consumer, one message per workspace | Keep the per-workspace cooldown; align Queue retries with it | −96 gateway invocations a day; adds Queue operations per workspace |
| `calendar-smart-schedule` | Workflow per workspace | Persist step results; finite attempts | −4 a day |
| `web-notification-batches`, `web-post-email-queue`, `web-topic-announcements`, `web-report-automation` | Queue consumers | Keep the existing row claims and send reconciliation; one attempt budget across Queue and claims | −336 a day; adds Queue operations per batch |
| `web-deadline-reminders` | Worker processor after the receipt check becomes an atomic claim | Make check-and-record one RPC before porting | −288 a day |
| `finance-exchange-rates` | Worker processor | One provider call a day | −1 a day |
| `infrastructure-sample-resources`, `infrastructure-docker-recovery-alerts` | Retire, pending owner decision | They read the retired Docker host | −1,728 a day if retired |

Ports that need Next.js-only effects (cache tags, React email rendering) keep a
small authenticated adapter in the owning app, called only when work happened,
until that app itself moves to Cloudflare. Durable business work never relies on
`ctx.waitUntil`.
